title: Golem Inductive Logic Programming Learns Human-Interpretable QSAR Drug-Binding Rules Matching X-Ray Crystallography
whyItMatters: Landmark PNAS study showing symbolic inductive logic programming (Golem) outperformed classical Hansch regression on DHFR drug-binding prediction while discovering stereochemical rules matching X-ray crystallography.
summary: Published in PNAS in December 1992, Ross D. King, Stephen Muggleton, Richard A. Lewis, and Michael J. E. Sternberg applied the inductive logic programming (ILP) system Golem to model structure-activity relationships of 55 trimethoprim analogues inhibiting E. coli dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR). Golem achieved higher predictive accuracy on unseen test molecules than standard Hansch linear regression and—crucially—induced readable first-order logic rules characterizing favored inhibitors by polarity, flexibility, and hydrogen bonding that independently agreed with crystallographic X-ray structures of the DHFR binding site. This work directly launched Ross King’s closed-loop Robot Scientist program (Adam and Eve).
technicalHighlights: Used relational first-order logic induction (Golem ILP) over molecular substituent properties rather than fixed-vector statistical features.
Outperformed standard Hansch QSAR regression on both training (44 compounds) and unseen test (11 compounds) DHFR inhibition.
Induced human-understandable chemical binding rules that independently matched the 3D stereochemistry observed in X-ray crystallography.
caveats: Evaluated on a modest 55-compound congeneric series of trimethoprim analogues.

scoreRationale.foundational: First demonstration that symbolic machine learning could outperform statistical QSAR and recover physically valid binding-site stereochemistry.
scoreRationale.ripple: Catalyzed relational machine learning in chemoinformatics and directly inspired Robot Scientists Adam and Eve.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in PNAS (Vol. 89, No. 23, pp. 11322–11326) with independent crystallographic corroboration.
scoreRationale.velocity: Automated rule discovery from empirical assay tables.
